Like everyone here, I've been excited for KSP2 since the announcement. I held off buying it when it released in Early Access because my PC couldn't run it and the community feedback. With a new PC and "For Science!" I decided to take the plunge.

I'm not having a great time.

The biggest problem for me is that there isn't joystick/controller support. That may seem like a nit, but considering that this is a spaceflight and flight sim, that's pretty core to the entire experience. If MS Flight Simulator released and required keyboard and mouse *only*, that would be pretty egregious.

While I don't love the UI, I fully acknowledge that that's more preference and comfort with KSP1 than a deficiency here, maybe. I think there are deficiencies, but honestly need to spend more time with it to know for sure.

There are other design choices that reduce immersion for me.

All of these can be changed and I imagine they will be, but at this point I'm having more frustrations than fun, and I'm really disappointed that they chose to limit user input to solely mouse and keyboard in a spaceflight simulator.

Do not buy in its current state. They've released way too soon for an extremely bare-bones game for early access.

Pros:
- Sound design is spectacular, the score, the sound effects, the ambience is fantastic, well done team.
- Space centre looks great, multiple launch locations are great, clouds are fine.

Issues:

- Performance issues, totally un-optimised. Not as bad as we were led to believe but still woeful.
- Innumerable silly, obvious bugs that could've been resolved before releasing.
- Clunky UI, very difficult to identify what's going on when most of the 'math' the game is doing is plain and simple incorrect numbers which make half the UI redundant at this time.
- Strut issues, no autostrut (that in itself is not a good fix for a more inherent issue).
- Overpriced considerably for the state this is in currently.
- Unclear roadmap and timelines. Over-reliance on 'we want to work with the community'... there are obvious things wrong currently and clear promises from pre-launch that should be prioritised. Work with the community once you're most of the way through your delivery plan.

0.2 "For Science" update: still a thumbs down. Many, many things have been fixed, but items that are critical to the core gameplay loop still remain. SAS control oscillation is still an issue. Delta-V calculations are all over the place. The vertical speed indicator does not work. You cannot fly rockets with no idea what's in the fuel tank or which way you're pointing.

This game is not cooked yet. There are serious issues with gameplay. Stages remain attached after jettisoning. Parts (particularly if radially attached to radial parts) randomly move around in the VAB. Flight path through another SOI is not shown, so you have no idea how you're approaching another body when planning maneuvers. VAB delta-V calcuations seem to randomly change. Most engines cause control oscillation when using SAS. Kerbals sometimes can't board spacecraft for reasons that are unclear. I haven't had issues with performance, but I have a very beefy processor (Ryzen 9 5900X) and ok-ish graphics (3060 RTX).

I get that this is "early access", but at the end of the day, numbers speak louder than words. As I contemplate the $50 I sunk into this thing, I begin to ask myself what they've been doing for the past 4 years. Fundamental features in the core gameplay loop, such as vehicle control and construction, are seriously broken.
Do not buy. The game is abandoned, the development team was dismantled during layoffs by parent companies. It should be removed from the store.

Okay, the game is now officially dead and buried.

We all need to understand that the Intercept Games devs have nothing to do with KSP 2 shutting down. They are the biggest victims here, not us who spent 30 odd euros on an unfinished game. The real devil is Take-Two Interactive whose executives decided they want to focus on the big titles - such as the GTA franchise - instead. Whenever a small studio is being backed by a large publisher, there are good chances of this happening.

It's very bad PR to release a game on early access and NOT to follow it all the way through. If you want to hold on to that warm fuzzy feeling of being able to pull the plug at a whim of a guy in a suit, do not sell the product before it has been finished.

I hope the KSP IP (that's a mouthful) will be bought by some respectable studio who cherishes on indie dev games and their ambitions to cater for niche players.

I've been a fan of a lot of the franchises backed up by Take-Two, but rest assured I will not spend a cent on anything they're going to publish. Yes, not even Civilization VII.

Don't get this game YET, buy KSP 1 instead, it is much more fleshed out and stable. i am confident that it will be amazing in the next few years, but it lacks a lot of features that the first game has, and has many issues with performance. However, slowly, the bugs are being fixed and the developers have planned all the other game's features, and many more down the line. The game was too ambitious to be released as early as it was. (i still love the developers but they have a long way to go)

Edit: publisher shut down development, never buy this game.
